questions.question: A student copies code from a GitHub project into his thesis and submits it as his own work without credit. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Passing off another's code or ideas as your own is plagiarism.

questions.question: An employee leaks a confidential manufacturing process to a rival firm. Which type of intellectual property is misappropriated?
questions.explanation: Confidential business processes are protected as trade secrets.

questions.question: An engineer reports her company's falsified safety tests to regulators after internal complaints are ignored. What is this act called?
questions.explanation: Reporting organizational wrongdoing to outside authorities is whistleblowing.

questions.question: A company modifies GPL-licensed code and sells binaries without releasing the source. What license requirement did it violate?
questions.explanation: GPL copyleft requires distributed derivatives to include source under the same license.

questions.question: A store uses a logo nearly identical to a famous brand's logo to confuse buyers. Which IP violation is this?
questions.explanation: Using a confusingly similar mark to identify goods is trademark infringement.

questions.question: A user downloads and installs a cracked copy of commercial software. What offense is this?
questions.explanation: Using cracked software is unauthorized copying, i.e., software piracy.

questions.question: A reviewer quotes two short paragraphs of a novel in a published critique with citation. Under what doctrine is this allowed?
questions.explanation: Brief quoted excerpts for criticism are a classic example of fair use.

questions.question: A website has images with no alt text and menus unreachable by keyboard. Which standard does it fail?
questions.explanation: Alt text and keyboard operability are core WCAG requirements.

questions.question: A firm dumps broken monitors containing lead into an ordinary landfill. What environmental problem does this create?
questions.explanation: Discarded electronics release hazardous substances when not recycled properly.

questions.question: An app secretly harvests users' contact lists without consent. Which ACM Code principle does this most directly breach?
questions.explanation: The ACM Code requires computing professionals to respect personal privacy.

questions.question: A developer must choose between meeting a deadline and shipping software she knows is unsafe. What is this situation called?
questions.explanation: Conflicting moral obligations create an ethical dilemma.

questions.question: A freelancer embeds MIT-licensed code in a closed-source app while keeping the copyright notice. Is this allowed?
questions.explanation: The MIT License permits proprietary reuse provided the notice is retained.

questions.question: A rival independently implements a method covered by a company's granted patent and is sued. Which IP right is the basis of the suit?
questions.explanation: Patents can be infringed even by independent reimplementation.

questions.question: A person registers a domain name mimicking a famous brand in order to resell it to the brand for profit. What is this practice called?
questions.explanation: Cybersquatting is bad-faith registration of trademark-related domain names.

questions.question: An office photocopies an entire textbook so employees do not have to buy copies. What is this best classified as?
questions.explanation: Wholesale copying to avoid purchase exceeds fair use and infringes copyright.
